summary.name: 10 Steps to Develop an Incident Response Plan
summary.one_liner: A Salesforce Engineering blog article giving ten practical steps for writing a security incident response plan (IRP) that teams will actually use rather than a compliance checkbox.
keywords: how to write incident response plan
use_cases: Writing an incident response plan from scratch
Defining what counts as a security incident
Setting up severity levels for security incidents
Building an escalation matrix and communications plan
Creating incident playbooks by incident type
summary.what_it_does: The article walks through ten steps: defining an incident with stakeholder signoff, scoping the plan, identifying and training stakeholders, documenting the response process phases, setting severity levels, building a communications plan and escalation matrix, creating playbooks per incident type, assembling the plan, testing it, and continuously improving it. It describes the Salesforce CSIRT's use of its own plan and includes example process steps, stakeholder group definitions, and severity factors. It recommends testing at least once per quarter, with a 60-minute tabletop exercise as an example.
notable: Written by the Salesforce CSIRT team, which says it uses and regularly tests its own IRP
Includes an example detect-phase workflow and stakeholder role definitions
Recommends including the Red Team as a stakeholder and using out-of-band communication
caveats: Advisory article, not a template or downloadable tool; plan content must be adapted to each organization
Gives no specific software tools beyond general references to a case management system and automated notification systems
